merge rules for two record types (component specs vs extracted design groups) with different keys and precedence; same loop shape only
one-off operator scripts (backfills, retention) each carry their own argparse and stack-output lookup on purpose, so a script runs alone from a checkout (the 5.28 duplicate audit kept them separate)
id-list / domain-list validators: same shape, each with its own limits, normalisation and 400 wording for its route
wire DTOs of two unrelated records (a voting session, a product document); equal only in being dict projections
page-settle polling in two separately bundled functions (design capture vs the web_reviews plugin, which cannot import lambda/shared)
views of two stored record types (source document, decision) with different fields
free-text validators of three routes (ballot note, assistant title, form submission): different limits, control-character rules and 400 wording per public contract
two cursor formats with their own size limit and error wording; sharing the 7-line base64-JSON decode would couple the feedback and Radar cursor contracts
caller display labels for different audiences (project setup editor, settings audit, username); same claim lookups, different fallbacks
optional-field validators with per-feature limits and messages; the settings rows already share dimension_config.bounded_text/bounded_list, the others are request contracts of their own routes
UpdateExpression builders and conditional updates on different rows (agent run fields vs brief card_state.#c paths; last-run stamp vs run-lock release), each with its own ServiceError message
access-row reads of two gates: different keys and projections, and each raises its own user-facing ServiceError text
the same 'unknown field / at least one field' preamble of two PUT bodies (brief preferences, onboarding), each with its own field list and value rules; a shared helper would save about four lines
component labels from two sources (GitHub paths vs Tailwind class names): same 4-line shape, different inputs
agent workflow nodes each check their own domain-API answer and raise their own NodeFailure text (one node = one readable file)
